One of India’s most revered pilgrimage sites Shree Mandir better known as the Jagannath Temple to the outside world in Puri is the epicentre of Odisha’s spiritual and cultural life. Built in the 12th century by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deba the temple is dedicated to Lord Jagannath, worshipped alongside his siblings Lord Balabhadra and Debi Subhadra. Its towering temple dominates the sacred skyline of Puri and has drawn devotees from across the world for centuries. The temple is especially famous for the grand Ratha Jatra or Chariot Festival as it is known worldwide. Massive wooden chariots carry the deities through the streets in a spectacle witnessed by millions. The temple kitchen considered among the largest in the world prepares Mahaprasad using traditional cooking methods passed down through generations. The State is accessible through international and domestic airports, major railway routes, and National Highways connecting eastern, northern, western, and southern regions of the country. Travelers can conveniently reach Odisha from different parts of India and abroad for tourism, pilgrimage, business, and cultural exploration. By Air By Rail By Road By Air Air travel is one of the fastest and most convenient ways to reach Odisha. The State is served by multiple airports, with Biju Patnaik International Airport (BBI) being the primary gateway to Odisha. Located approximately 6 kilometers from the city center, the airport offers regular domestic and international connectivity to cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Raipur. Other operational airports in Odisha include: Veer Surendra Sai Airport (Domestic) Major tourist destinations such as Puri are easily accessible from Bhubaneswar by road. Taxi, cab, and bus services are available from the airport for onward travel. Visitors are advised to book flight tickets in advance during peak tourism and festive seasons. Content: Skip to Main Content DISCOVER EXPERIENCE PLAN YOUR TRIP BOOK NOW EN English Hindi Odia Heritage Properties LUXURY HERITAGE STAYS ACROSS ODISHA / Accommodations / Heritage Properties Overview Experiences Heritage Stays Videos Journey Continues LUXURY & HERITAGE STAYS Where Every Palace Tells a Story Odisha's heritage stays invite travelers to experience a side of the state that few destinations can offer. These historic palaces, forts and royal residences, many of which continue to be home to the erstwhile royal families, open a window into centuries of history, architecture and tradition. Each property reflects the character of its region. Nestled beside rivers, amidst forests or overlooking rolling hills, these heritage homes have been thoughtfully restored to preserve their original charm while offering the comforts of a memorable stay. From elegant Victorian mansions and riverside palaces to secluded hunting lodges and historic fort residences, every destination has a story waiting to be discovered. A stay at these heritage properties is about more than beautiful architecture. It is an opportunity to walk through grand courtyards and Durbar Halls, admire antique collections and family heirlooms, savor recipes rooted in royal kitchens, and engage with traditions that continue to thrive through the generations. It was here that Emperor Ashoka witnessed the devastation of war and embraced the path of peace and Buddhism, transforming from the feared "Chandashoka" to the compassionate "Dharmashoka". About the Show The Dhauli Light & Sound Show is a spectacular 35-minute 3D projection mapping experience that transforms the white Peace Pagoda into a living canvas of history. Through immersive visuals, dramatic narration and music, the show retells the story of the Kalinga War, Ashoka's remorse, and the rise of Buddhism from the land of Odisha. Set against the tranquil backdrop of the Daya River, the experience combines history, spirituality and cutting-edge technology in a deeply moving evening attraction. Once every year, Lord Jagannath, along with his brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra, leaves the sanctum of the Shree Mandir and comes out onto the streets of Puri to meet his devotees. From the Ratnasinghasan, the Lord is carried by his Sevayats in the ceremonial procession known as Pahandi, swaying gracefully to the rhythm of brass gongs, cymbals, conches, and devotional chants as waves of faith fill the air. This is not a festival you merely witness, you become part of it. People pull the chariots together, walk alongside the deities, and chant with strangers who feel like family for the day. The towering wooden chariots move slowly through Bada Danda, the Grand Road of Puri, transforming the city into a river of devotion. The story begins after Deba Snana Purnima, when the deities are believed to fall ill following their ceremonial bath. They rest in seclusion for a few days, cared for like members of a family. Once they recover, they set out for their annual journey to the Gundicha Temple, believed to be their aunt’s home. The journey feels deeply familiar and human, a homecoming filled with affection, celebration, and togetherness. From distant Arctic landscapes and Central Asian wetlands, thousands of migratory birds arrive at Odisha’s great lagoon, transforming its waters into one of the most spectacular birding landscapes in Asia. The National Chilika Bird Festival celebrates this extraordinary annual migration and positions Odisha as one of India’s premier birdwatching destinations. Held at Mangalajodi on the northern fringes of Chilika Lake and Nalabana – the marine bird sanctuary within the lagoon, the festival brings together birders, photographers, conservationists, researchers, nature enthusiasts, and travellers from across India and beyond. It is an invitation to experience the wonder of migration, the richness of wetland biodiversity, and the remarkable conservation story of Chilika. Every year during winter, nearly one million migratory birds representing over 200 species arrive at Chilika along the Central Asian Flyway.
